lead: Salem's winters are long and wet, and the Willamette River runs right past downtown. Steady rain, ice storms and crawl space moisture cause most of its water damage.
risk: winter rain leaks, ice storms and river flooding
risk_short: winter rain, ice storms, river floods
why: Salem gets most of its rain from October to April, often in long, steady storms. Roofs with moss, clogged gutters and worn flashing let water in slowly, and the leak may not show up until a ceiling stains. Many Salem homes sit over crawl spaces that stay damp all winter. In February 1996, warm rain on snow sent the Willamette over its banks and flooded low parts of Salem.

Ice storms are a newer worry. In January 2024, freezing rain coated the Willamette Valley in ice. Trees and power lines fell across Salem, and many homes lost power for days. Fallen limbs opened roofs, and frozen pipes split in cold houses. About half of Salem homes were built before 1980, and older supply lines and roofs are more likely to fail in storms like that.

tips: Clean moss off the roof and clear gutters each fall.
Add a vapor barrier and keep crawl space vents working.
Have large trees near the house checked by an arborist.
Insulate pipes in crawl spaces before cold snaps.
areas: Calls come from Downtown, Grant, West Salem, South Salem, Highland, Fairmount Hill, Sunnyslope and Northgate, plus Keizer, Turner and Independence.

faq.q: Why does my Salem ceiling only leak in winter?
faq.a: Most Salem rain falls in winter, often for days at a time. Worn shingles, moss, clogged gutters and loose flashing let water in slowly. The leak may follow a rafter before it shows up as a stain. A roofer should find the entry point, and DryFlare can dry the attic and ceiling.
